A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Avoiding Catastrophe in Online Learning by Asking for Help. All 32 pages in each version, including equations, algorithms, Table 1, Figure 1, and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports theoretical algorithms, constructions, bounds, and proofs, including throughout its appendices. Table 1 is a conceptual comparison and Figure 1 illustrates a proof construction; neither reports empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v6 likewise contains theoretical results and proofs throughout the main text and appendices, without original experiments, simulations, user studies, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: The Hedge-based querying algorithm, one-versus-rest extension, and bucketing algorithm are retained. Algorithm 1's separate empty-history check is absorbed into an explicit empty-minimum convention. Algorithm 3's Pi_y corrections align its cover setup with the per-action procedure already described and invoked in v5.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or reports training or evaluation tasks. The theoretical input spaces and policy-class examples are retained.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. Table 1's conceptual comparison with standard online learning is unchanged.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental evaluation protocol. No data splits, evaluation metrics, sample sizes, or experimental budgets are introduced or revised.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, or case studies. The analytical threshold-policy example in Appendix D and necessity argument for local generalization in Appendix E retain their substance.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Probabilities and expectations appear in theoretical analyses, without changes to empirical uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries appear in either version, and the stated main and appendix theorem conclusions are retained. The changed intermediate proof expressions are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Lemma B.6 corrects the intermediate bound for the expected size of Q-hat_1 from a log(1/epsilon) factor to log(T + 1/epsilon), matching Lemma B.1. Its query-count derivation also removes a separately counted first-query +1 using the empty-minimum convention. These are localized proof revisions; the stated theorem bounds and substantive assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: general impossibility with sublinear queries, and subconstant regret with sublinear mentor queries under the stated learnability and local-generalization assumptions.

C2.justification: Sections 5.2 and 6 retain the same interpretations and limitations concerning input encodings, nearest-neighbor access, computational efficiency, finite VC dimension with fully adversarial inputs, and extensions to MDPs.

D1.justification: Section 3 newly specifies that a minimum over an empty set is infinite, explicitly documenting edge-case handling for Algorithm 1's distance-based query test. This clarifies implementation of the existing procedure; algorithm parameters and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Adding the year to the existing Barman et al. citation and correcting reference titles, capitalization, and page information are bibliographic repairs, not new related work.

P1.justification: v6 makes localized grammatical, notation, and bibliographic corrections, adds the empty-minimum convention, and streamlines Lemma B.6's explanation. Sections and Appendices A–E retain their organization, without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 1, including their captions, are unchanged. Small line-wrap and spacing changes affect algorithm and proof pages, while bibliography corrections alter the reference-page break. The overall layout and display organization are retained.

improvement.justification: v6 improves local mathematical consistency by correcting Lemma B.6's logarithmic bound, clarifying empty-set handling, and repairing Algorithm 3's inconsistent policy-class references. Together with the editorial corrections, these changes make the existing arguments and procedures easier to follow. The gains are limited because the contributions, theorem guarantees, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
